correctness.rationale: Coordinate sign changes reduce the image to one-dimensional Walsh eigenspaces, with necessary parity and degree bounds. For 1<=j<=d-1 a planar harmonic times linear factors evaluates to a nonzero multiple of each desired Walsh character. Explicit harmonic polynomials give the constant mode at all even degrees except two. At degree two the cubical average vanishes by the harmonic trace condition. At degree d the full product of coordinates works, but at degree d+2 every full-odd harmonic is x_1...x_d times a trace-zero quadratic in squared variables and hence evaluates to zero. These cases exhaust 0<=ell<=d+2. Exact Gegenbauer-kernel calculations independently corroborate every eigenvalue zero/nonzero for d=6..10, 505 instances; finite tests are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The natural sampling map from a single spherical-harmonic eigenspace to the vertices of a regular Euclidean cube has an exact, uniform rank classification through the first post-saturation levels. The exceptional absence of the degree-d Walsh character at harmonic degree d+2 causes a one-dimensional rank reversal after three fully saturated parity degrees; this is a motivated identifiability obstruction, not a mere isolated numeric computation. The constructive proof gives explicit realizations for all allowable sampling patterns.
